newsitem.title: GERMANY: Berlin agrees to keep remant of Berlin Wall.
newsitem.headline: Berlin agrees to keep remant of Berlin Wall.

text.p: A small remnant of the Berlin Wall left standing as part of a monument to the Cold War barrier will not be torn down in order to clear a path to an adjoining cemetery, city and church officials said on Wednesday.
Church leaders wanted to tear down part of a 200-metre long section of the Berlin Wall near Bernauer Strasse, saying there were mass graves of German soldiers from World War Two lying beneath it.

But the city said it had reached an agreement with the church leaders to maintain the full section of the wall because of its historical importance. The cemetery will be included in a monument at the Wall that is to be built in May.

Most of the 150-km long Berlin Wall that separated East and West Berlin between 1961 and 1989 were removed within months of the Wall's breaching in November 1989. But tourism to Berlin has since slumped and many local business leaders have urged the city to maintain the pieces still left.

Several large slabs of the Wall on Bernauer Strasse were dragged away two weeks ago after Lutheran minister Johannes Hildebrandt called for a memorial to mark the site where he said soldiers killed in the final Berlin battles of World War Two were buried.
Hildebrandt's claims were dismissed by several local politicians who said he had failed to provide any proof that the graves were directly underneath that section of the Wall.

Bernauer Strasse was one of the most famous parts of the Wall. Many people jumped from buildings along the eastern section of the Wall when it was first built. Two would-be refugees died in such attempts.
